title: Community Pharmacy
description: Community pharmacy post-inspection checklist / auditing checklist

items.text: Valid license (check legality status and license number; note issue date)
License displayed in a clear place (check originality)
The name of the pharmacy is conspicuously displayed near public entrances
Accessibility of entrance to people with disability
Promotional materials like posters on windows, doors or exterior parts
Cleanliness and maintenance of the premises
Waste accumulations and depot surrounding the pharmacy
Storage areas must be self-contained, with no connection to doors or windows of other premises
Dispensing area maintained in good repair with washable walls and floors
Dispensing area is clean, tidy, and uncluttered (check regular cleaning schedules)
Medicines must not be accessible by self-service
All medicines are stored within the professional area
No medicine shelved with any other products (check fridge and sample rows)
Access to dispensing area is strictly controlled
Size and layout allow effective communication, direct supervision, safe and efficient workflow
Medicines dispensed with appropriate counseling and recorded in logbook
Keep individual information of chronic patients and medication profiles for each refill visit
Medicines prescribed based on STG and dispensed based on National Formulary
Medicines labeled before dispensing to patient
Appropriate area for counseling of patients
Shelving arrangement is alphabetical, pharmacological, or logical
Written SOP for compounding available and displayed in CPD room
Type of products prepared and source of ingredients checked
Neatness of compounding room and cleaning procedures
Compounding done by licensed pharmacist (or checked by pharmacist)
Compounded medicines recorded in a logbook
Standard prescription used for non-NPS medicines
Record of prescription registration book for prescription-only medicines
Use filled, signed prescriptions (check patient, facility, medication, professional details, legibility, completeness, correctness)
Use valid prescriptions (not copied, forged, or plain paper; check signatures and license numbers)
On average, 2-3 medicines prescribed and dispensed per prescription
Prescription-only medicines not dispensed without prescription
Check frequency of prescriptions from given facility or prescriber
Check interactions and/or contraindications in dispensed medicines

sections.title: Adverse Drug Reaction and Product Defect Reporting

items.text: Prepaid yellow page / ADE reporting format available
Check any reported ADR and product quality defects
Bin and stock cards are updated
Availability of vouchers, sales tickets, and dispensing registers (legal and timely)
Proper recording, use, and filing of vouchers, sales tickets, and registers
Record date and quantity received on stock and bin cards
Check FIFO or LIFO flow of medicines
Check beginning and ending stock balance and purchase amounts
Trace source, legality, and batch numbers using invoices
Check for non-pharmacist engagement in purchasing
Check availability and source of program medicines
Suppliers, wholesalers, or distributors are licensed in Ethiopia
All records kept and prescriptions kept for at least two years
Orders, storage, preparation, sale, delivery, and disposal recorded and maintained
All unfit-for-use (damaged or expired) medicines recorded
Stock on hand and dispensed controlled substances recorded and maintained
Separate locked room or cabinet (key kept with head pharmacist, permanently affixed)
NPS prescriptions not used to prescribe other medicines
NPS and other medicines not prescribed together (single prescription for single NPS drug)
NPS prescription papers maintained for at least five years
Use filled and officially signed NPS prescriptions (check patient/facility stamp, serial number)
Submit regular consumption and stock reports to appropriate regulatory organ
All records of NPS stored securely
Licensed pharmacists available in the pharmacy (check HR files)
All pharmacy personnel wear name tags with clear responsibility and profession
Head pharmacist has at least four years of work experience
Pharmacy personnel wear appropriate, neat gowns different from other staff
Availability of current editions of dispensing manual, national treatment guideline, and national formulary
Availability of other reputable reference books
Availability of telephone for medicines information provision
Medicines stored correctly under conditions not affected by moisture, temperature, or light (check room temperature, To, RH patterns, thermohygrometer)
No medicines stored on floors, stairs, and passageways
Storage area in good repair with washable walls
Damaged or expired stocks stored separately from usable stock
Liquid products placed on lower or bottom shelves
Store flammable liquids in original containers
Functional BP, height, weight measurement, and blood glucose devices (checked calibration)
Suitable and hygienic means of counting tablets and capsules
Dispensing labels and envelopes with appropriate information
Calibrated and functional fire extinguisher available (check inspection records)
Smoking policy / no smoking labels available
Conducting self-assessment quarterly and reporting (scoring, strengths, gaps, action plan sent to ZHD/Woreda/Town regulatory body)
Pharmacy service provision complies against standards (check score and verification feedback)

sections.title: Tracer Medicines for Sampling during the Audit

items.text: Antibiotics (Ceftriaxone inj, Tetracycline 250mg cap, Vancomycin, etc.)

title: Medium Dental Specialty Clinic
description: Medium dental specialty clinic licensing checklist

sections.title: 4. Size and Area of Facility Work Rooms

items.text: Reception / Card room ? 1 room (16 sq. m.)
Examination and Treatment room ? 2 rooms (12 sq. m. each)
Dental Laboratory room ? 1 (as per dental lab standard)
Cleaning and Sterilization room ? 1 room (8 sq. m.)
Toilet room (Male & Female) ? 2 rooms (8 sq. m. each)
Store room for medical supplies ? 1 room (5 sq. m.)
Dental unit with dental chair, dental stool
Materials & instruments to keep area free from moisture & improve visibility
Rotating & hand cutting instruments (bone rongeurs, files, elevators)
Mandibular forceps for anterior & posterior teeth extraction
Maxillary forceps for anterior & posterior teeth extraction
Forceps & elevators for Maxillary and Mandibular root extraction
Different pans use for disinfection & sterilization
Different operatory cabinets, drum, kidney dish
Light curing unit with composite materials
The dental specialty clinic shall be directed by licensed dental surgeon.
The dental specialty clinic shall provide service at outpatient/ambulatory level only.
Emergency care specific to the dentistry with a qualified staff shall be available during working hours.
The dental specialty clinic shall have a program of continuous quality improvement for the service.
The dental specialty clinic shall provide or facilitate training to their staffs.

The dental specialty clinic shall display the following at a visible place: a) List of services available in the clinic during working hours and after working hours; b) List of professionals working in the clinic during and after working hours; c) Updated list of various fees and prices.
The dental specialty clinic facilities shall be well marked and easily accessible for persons with disability.
All patient care rooms shall be provided with running water supply and functional hand-washing basin.
A dental specialty clinic where functional units are at different floors shall have a mechanism of accessing all functioning rooms horizontally, either by stairs and ramp or stairs and elevator.
The dental specialty clinic shall have an established system for verbal and written communication about patient care.
The number and type of technical staff shall be determined by the volume and type of work carried out (Workload Analysis).

Dental Specialty clinic level shall be available at least during the regular working hours based on its scope of practice. This includes restorative services (advice, support and treatment for patients referred from primary care; use, processing and interpretation of intraoral periapical x-rays; diagnosis and management of common dental caries and acute tooth pain; single- and compound-walled caries; class I?V restorations; pulp capping; veneering; anterior pin-supported restorations; fractured-tooth restorations; and referral to the next health tier); endodontic services (diagnosis, x-ray use, endodontic emergencies, anterior and single-rooted tooth treatment, incomplete root formation, vital and non-vital bleaching, retrograde filling, and referral); prosthetic services (assessment and treatment planning for missing teeth, bite registration, use of an articulator, implant-related diagnosis and intervention, artificial prosthesis, and fixed/removable partial dentures); orthodontic services (x-rays and interpretation, assessment and referral, preservation or regain of leeway space, removable orthodontics and appropriate fixed treatment); periodontal therapy (gingival hyperplasia, scaling and root planing, periodontal inflammation/infection and referral); minor oral surgery including exodontias (dento-alveolar infection, referral for complicated facial-space infection/fracture, exodontia for pediatric and adult patients, simple facial/oral soft-tissue injuries, uncomplicated dento-alveolar fracture and simple non-displaced mandibular fracture); and oral health education.

The dental surgeon (DDM) shall not perform removable complete denture, fixed complete denture, and maxillofacial prosthodontics, as these procedures shall be performed by specialists with advanced training.

The dental specialty clinic shall provide: care of ambulatory patients and follow-up of ambulatory patients; preventive and health promotion services; and care for patients with chronic illnesses and follow-ups.

Patient assessment at the dental clinic shall include: a) comprehensive medical and social history; b) physical examination including vital signs (BP, PR, RR, temperature, pain assessment), height and weight, and clinical examination pertinent to the illness; c) diagnostic impression; d) laboratory and imaging services when indicated; and e) other medical workups when indicated.
The range of relevant treatment options and the clinical impression shall be fully described to the client and/or their families and documented on the patient?s medical record accordingly.

Information in the dental record shall be complete with respect to the patient?s history, physical examination, oral (intra- and extra-oral) examination, diagnosis, diagnostic procedures, medication administration, and treatment to facilitate continuity of care.
The dental specialty clinic shall have a system for the nurse to take vital signs and other necessary assessments to make the patient ready for dental service.
The dental service shall be provided in accordance with infection prevention standards.

The dental specialty clinic shall have a functional referral system including: a list of conditions indicative for urgent referral; SOP for selection of cases for referral; procedure for referring patients directly to respective higher services; list of potential referral sites with contact address (referral directory); referral forms; referral tracing mechanism (linkage); feedback-providing mechanism; and documentation of referred clients.
The outpatient service shall be well marked and easily accessible for disabled clients, elderly people, children, and pregnant mothers.
The patient waiting area and corridor shall be ventilated and child-friendly.
All rooms for patient care shall promote patient dignity and privacy. Outpatient rooms shall have adequate light and ventilation.
The dental clinics shall have IEC and entertaining materials in the waiting area.
Reception, Recording & Waiting area for oral health education ? 1 room, 20 sq. m.
Examination and treatment room with dental unit ? 1 room, 12 sq. m.
Dental x-ray room (optional if the machine is not separate from the dental unit) ? 1, as per ERPA.
Panoramic x-ray room ? 1, as per ERPA.
Dental laboratory (optional) ? 1, as per dental laboratory standard requirement.
Cleaning and Sterilization room & store ? 1 room, 8 sq. m.
Staff or changing room ? 1 room, 6 sq. m.
Burnisher (ball type, football type, interproximal type) (optional)
Light curing unit with composite materials
Kit for friction lock retention pin
Matrix band and retainer (metallic & celluloid, different sizes)
Materials & instruments to keep area free from moisture & improve visibility
Micro motor with hand piece and burs
Forceps for Dental Extractions (Deciduous & Permanent teeth)
Impression Trays for upper & lower jaws
Preformed temporary stainless steel & polycarbonate crowns
Arch wires (Niti & Stainless steel in various dimensions)
Mandrels, Carborundum, Silica, Crocus discs and stones
Local anesthesia (Spray, Lidocaine multi-dose, Cartridges with/without adrenaline)
Medical record shall be maintained in written form for every patient seen at all points of care.
The specialty clinics shall maintain individual medical records in a manner to ensure accuracy and easy retrieval.
The specialty clinic shall have a unique medical record per patient.
The specialty clinic shall have a queue management system.

The specialty clinic shall have a written policy and procedure including: procedures for record completion; conditions, procedures, and fees for releasing medical information; and procedures for protection of medical record information against loss, tampering, alteration, destruction, or unauthorized use.
Any medical record shall be kept confidential, available only for use by authorized persons or as otherwise permitted by law.
All entries in the patient?s medical record shall be written legibly in permanent ink, dated, and signed by the recording person.

Each medical record shall at least contain: identification (name, age, sex, address); history, physical examination, investigation results, and diagnosis; medication, procedure, and consultation notes; name and signature of treating physician and date; and consent form where applicable, signed by the patient. If someone other than the patient signs, the reason and the signer?s relationship to the patient shall be indicated on the form.
Any consent form for medical treatment that the patient signs shall be printed in an understandable format and written in clear, legible, and non-technical language.
There shall be a mechanism for medical record controlling and tracing whenever patient medical records are taken from and returned to the central medical record room.
There shall be a mechanism to make medical records with appointments ready for use and return seen cards to the central medical record room within 24 hours.
If the patient is provided with medical certificates, copies of certificates and other records shall be documented and/or recorded on the original medical record.
The specialty clinics shall establish a procedure for removal of inactive medical records from the central medical record room.
Medical records shall be destroyed as per the law by using techniques that assure confidentiality. Records active for more than ten years shall not be destroyed.

The premises for the medical record room shall be suitable for movement. Medical records shall be shelved a minimum of 3?4 inches from any outside wall, with the lowest shelf at least 3?4 inches off the floor; the top of the top shelf shall never be used to store records.
The medical record room shall have adequate space for central filing, workspace, archive space, and supply/storage room.
The medical record room shall be built far from fire and any damaging sources.
There shall be a room/area for archiving dead files until they are permanently destroyed.
There shall be a full-time custodian/medical record personnel/Health Information Technician with basic computer skill and ability to organize.
The specialty clinics shall provide basic training on medical record keeping to the staffs.

The medical record room shall have a minimum of the following: shelves; Master Patient Index boxes; computer and printer; standard reporting formats; cart; ladder; patient folder; MPI cards; log book; and fire extinguisher.
The health promotion service shall be available in the dental clinic.
The specialty clinics shall plan, schedule, coordinate, lead, and monitor a minimum of specialty clinic-specific health promotion activities.
The specialty clinics shall make sure that health promotion practice provides unbiased and evidence-based information.
The health promotion activity of the specialty clinics shall respect the national health policy, legislations, protocols, and directives.
A health professional shall be designated to coordinate health promotion activities.
The specialty clinics shall have a waiting area at reception with audio-visual health promotion materials.
The specialty clinics? technical manager shall take the lead to identify priority conditions and prepare or avail promotion materials.
The roles and responsibilities of the designee in relation to health promotion shall be specified in his/her job descriptions.
Health professionals shall provide health education in their specific discipline.
The specialty clinic shall have audio-visual and printed material (TV set, DVD/VCD, radio, tape-recorded) at the reception area.
All activities performed for infection prevention shall comply with the national infection prevention and control guidelines.
Infection prevention and control shall be effectively and efficiently governed and managed according to IPC guidelines.

The specialty clinics shall identify procedures and processes associated with infection risk and implement strategies to reduce infection risk, including appropriate use of PPE; equipment cleaning; sterilization, in particular of invasive equipment as appropriate; separation of patients with communicable diseases; disposal of infectious waste and body fluids; disposal of sharps and needles; and aseptic techniques for invasive procedures.
IPC training shall be provided for all specialty clinic staff as recommended by the national infection prevention and control guidelines.

At a minimum, the following procedures shall be maintained: decontamination and reprocessing of medical devices (instrument processing); environmental cleaning; specialty clinic waste management; standard precautions; transmission-based precautions; hand hygiene; personal protective equipment/PPE; and sharp and injection safety.

The specialty clinics shall train all staff on how to minimize exposure to blood-borne infections and provide documented evidence. Training shall include immediate first aid; reporting and monitoring protocols; evaluation of the PEP program; reporting exposures; and counseling and testing for exposed staff.
The specialty clinics shall provide basic or refresher IPC training for permanent and new staff at least once per year.
Infectious and non-infectious medical wastes shall be handled and managed.
The specialty clinics? environment shall be clean and safe. There shall be access to continuous, safe, and ample water supply.
The specialty clinics shall routinely clean and sanitize patient areas and waiting rooms at least twice daily and more whenever needed.
Sewage disposal shall be according to the Specialty Clinic Waste Management National Directive. The specialty clinics shall have a functional sewerage system and only flushing toilet system.

The housekeeping service shall have the following sanitary activities: basic cleaning such as dusting, sweeping, polishing, and washing; special cleaning of different types of floors, walls and ceilings, doors and windows, furniture and fixtures, and Venetian blinds; cleaning and maintenance of toilet and shower; water treatment, filtering and purification.
Infectious and non-infectious medical waste containers shall be leak proof, have tight-fitting covers, and be kept clean and in good repair until disposal.
Reusable containers for infectious medical waste and general medical waste shall be thoroughly washed and decontaminated each time.

Wastes shall be segregated. Segregation of specialty clinic waste shall include: separating different types of waste; providing colored waste receptacles specifically suited for each category; segregation at the source (such as ward bedside, OR, and laboratory); and using a three-bin system.
Treatment or disposal of infectious medical waste shall be performed by one or more approved methods.

Approved methods include incineration; incineration or interment of recognizable human anatomical remains unless burial at an approved landfill is authorized; chemical sterilization; gas sterilization; discharge via an approved sewerage system; steam sterilization; and secure landfill.
Specialty clinic waste that is not infectious shall be disposed of according to the Health Care Waste Management National Directive.
The facility shall have a waste management plan for all specialty clinic wastes.
The waste management plan shall include segregation, storage, disposal, treatment, and transport of medical waste.
In the housekeeping service, the types and sources of unwanted odors in the specialty clinic premises shall be identified, controlled, and removed.
If the specialty clinic does not have its own housekeeping and maintenance services, there shall be a contract agreement with external organizations.
All areas of the specialty clinic, including the building and grounds, shall be kept clean and orderly.
The specialty clinic shall conduct regular routine, preventive, and corrective maintenance for all facilities and operating systems (e.g., electrical, water, and ventilation).

There shall be written protocols and procedures for medical equipment maintenance, including a plan for preventive and curative maintenance, replacements, upgrades, and new equipment; safe disposal procedures; an effective tracking system to monitor maintenance activity; and a method to ensure diagnostic equipment operates with predicted specificity and sensitivity.
The specialty clinic shall comply with the National Fire Protection standard.

Fire extinguishers shall be visually inspected at least monthly; fully inspected at least annually; recharged, repaired, and hydro-tested as required by the manufacturer; and labeled with the date of the last inspection.

No flammable cleaning agents or other flammable liquids or gases shall be stored in any area of the specialty clinic except in a properly fire-rated and ventilated storage area specifically designed for such storage.
A reliable drinking-water point shall be accessible for staff, patients, and attendants at all times.
Ample and potable water services shall be available 24 hours a day and 365 days a year through regular or alternate sources.
A reliable water point, with soap or a suitable alternative, shall be available at all clinical service areas.
If rainwater and mains supply are both used, mains water shall be isolated from the rainwater system by a valve mechanism or tap.
If the specialty clinic has ground water, there shall be a written policy and procedures for ground water treatment.
Water in tanks shall be protected from sunlight.
Plastic tanks should be kept out of the sun or painted.
Separate space shall be provided for storage of housekeeping equipment and supplies.
Adequate space shall be available for service-specific janitors? closets and cleaning equipment and supplies, maintained separately and not used for cleaning other locations.
Separate janitors? closets and cleaning equipment shall be maintained for surgical suites; laboratories, radiology, offices, locker rooms and other areas; and patient areas.
The specialty clinic shall have an alternate emergency power supply.

The specialty clinic waste management system shall have a functional sewerage system including septic tank, solid waste storage room/area, plumbing setup stores as appropriate, and flushing toilets/VIP latrine.

The specialty clinic shall have the following personnel: an environmental health professional/designated officer; a general maintenance technologist/technician (optional); housekeeping staff such as cleaners and waste handlers; and a plumber as appropriate.

sections.title: Infection Prevention and Control Equipment and Supplies

items.text: The specialty clinic shall ensure that equipment and supplies necessary for infection prevention are available.
The specialty clinic shall have a reserve electrical generator.
Waste management equipment and supplies shall include color-coded bins, waste baskets, garbage bin, plastic garbage bags, safety boxes, and needle crusher (optional).

Cleaning products shall include floor-cleaning brush (optional), plastic drum, wheelbarrow, water trolley, ladder, scraping pump (optional), spraying pump (optional), Flit pump, broom, dust mop, floor-wiping brush, counter brush, ceiling brush, glass-cleaning/wiping brush, scrapers, dustbin paddles, plastic mug, rat-trapping cage, bed pan washer, cleaning towel, and plastic bucket.

Instrument-processing supplies shall include autoclaves/steam sterilizers, test strips, oven, drums of different sizes, storage shelves for medical equipment, chemicals and disinfectants, and brushes.
Hand-hygiene supplies shall include hand-washing sinks, alcohol-based hand rub, faucet, paper towels, tap water/water container, and soap.
Personal protective equipment shall include gown, heavy-duty glove, surgical glove, plastic apron, boots, examination glove, goggles, different masks, head cover, and face shield.
The medium clinic shall be directed by a General Practitioner / Public Health Officer / BSc Nurse / BSc Midwife.
The clinic shall provide service only at outpatient/ambulatory level at least during working hours.
Emergency care with qualified staff shall be available during government working hours.
The medium clinic shall avail updated reference materials, treatment guidelines, and manuals for common diseases.
Diseases under national surveillance shall be notified to the FMOH through the proper reporting channel.
The medium clinic shall have at a minimum the required health personnel and support staff (see staffing requirements below).
The medium clinic shall conduct workload analysis.
The medium clinic shall assign a quality focal person to improve quality of service deliveries.
The medium clinic shall provide or facilitate training to their staff.

The medium clinic shall display in a visible place: list of available services (during and after working hours); list of working professionals (during and after working hours); and an updated list of fees and prices.
The medium clinic facilities shall be well marked and easily accessible for persons with disability.
Potential sources of accidents shall be identified and acted upon, including slippery floors, doorways, and footsteps.
All patient care rooms shall be provided with a functional hand-washing basin.

Internal surfaces (floors, walls, and ceilings) shall be smooth, impervious, free from cracks, easy to clean and decontaminate, and made of non-combustible materials or materials with high fire resistance and low flame-spread characteristics.
Circulation ways and sub-corridors shall be a minimum of 2 m wide.
Patient-serving corridors shall not be less than 2 m wide.
Glass doors shall be marked to avoid accidental collision.
Multi-floor facilities shall provide access to all functional rooms by stairs and ramp or stairs and elevator.

Area for burial pit ? As required

title: Primary Clinic
description: Private primary clinic inspection / supervision checklist

items.text: The primary clinic shall have a minimum of the following premises set up (see details below).
The Primary clinic shall have direct access to examination room for emergency.
The Primary clinic shall have hand washing basin/ facility at examination and treatment room.
There shall be a note in a visually accessible area that details the facility working hours and list of services available.
Reception, Registry / Recording & Waiting area ? 1 room; 12 sq. m
Treatment / procedure / injection room ? 1 room; 12 sq. m
The primary clinic shall have the required staffing (see detailed staffing requirements below).

items.text: Infectious and medical wastes shall be handled and managed according to recent guidelines.
Segregation of health care waste (separate types, colored receptacles, at source, 3-bin system).
The clinic shall have a medical waste management plan (storage, segregation, transport, disposal).
Supportive sanitation measures (clean water, hand hygiene, sterilization, PPE alternatives).
Sanitary system (flushing toilets, plumbing stores, sanitary office, incinerator, pits, secured solid waste area).
The primary clinic shall officially designate staff in charge of handling waste on a regular basis.
Equipment and supplies required for sanitation activities: incinerator, safety boxes, leak-proof containers, trolley, PPE, autoclave, pressure cooker, cleaning solutions, mops, and dustbins.

sections.title: 6. Equipment, Instruments & Consumables - a) Equipment & Instruments

items.text: The ophthalmology specialty clinic shall provide ophthalmology services at outpatient level only, at least during regular working hours.
Minor surgical procedures with local and regional anesthesia shall follow the minor surgical standards in this document.
Optometry service shall be available in the clinic.
Ophthalmology services shall be provided by a licensed ophthalmologist.
Client medical records, registers, and reporting formats shall follow the national system.
A comprehensive medical and social history shall be obtained for each eye patient.
Physical eye examination shall include visual acuity, blood pressure when necessary, and clinical examination pertinent to the illness.
Eye examination shall include slit-lamp and/or fundo-ophthalmoscope examination.
A diagnostic impression shall be documented.
Visual field testing shall be included in the eye assessment.
Intraocular pressure (IOP) shall be measured by tonometry.
Keratometry and ocular ultrasound shall be available when indicated (optional).
The ophthalmology / eye clinic shall have the outpatient service rooms listed below.
A corridor at least 6 m long shall be available for visual acuity examination.
All rooms shall have a wash basin with running water.
Reception, recording, and waiting area: 1 room, 30 sq. m.
Examination room(s) with slit lamp: 1 room, 12 sq. m.
Procedure / minor surgery room with scrub room: 1 room, 20 sq. m.
Observation room with 2 couches: 1 room, 16 sq. m.
Keratometry and ultrasound examination room: 1 room, 20 sq. m (optional).
Staff / patient toilets (male and female): 2 toilets, 4 sq. m each.
Medical supplies store room: 1 room, area as required.
The clinic shall be directed by a licensed ophthalmologist with at least two years of relevant clinical experience, available during all working hours.
The nurse practicing in the eye clinic shall be trained and experienced in ophthalmology services.
The eye clinic shall have the required minimum staffing listed below.
Optometrist / Refractionist: 1 if optometry service is available (conditional).
The clinic shall have the diagnostic equipment and instruments listed below.
Trial set with trial frame (children and adults)
Probing set / lacrimal dilator and probe
Sutures of different sizes and types
